conversation.text:
Police: Who was the person you spoke with on the afternoon of February 3?
Respondent: As you can see, we don’t have many permanent staff in our office, so I basically handle all the phone calls myself.
Respondent: Are you referring to Ms. Shen Huijing? The afternoon of the 3rd?
Respondent: We generally don’t make calls during working hours, for fear that they might have opinions and think we are monitoring their work... And it’s even less likely that we would call her in the afternoon.
Respondent: Ah, we did make one call. There was nothing particularly important.
Respondent: In a few days, there will be a Best Housekeeping Service Worker Commendation Conference.
Respondent: I called to ask if she could come and attend. There are over 100 housekeeping service workers registered with us, but not a single one is willing to come.
Respondent: But after the call, I regretted it. She definitely won’t come.
Respondent: Ms. Shen Huijing, you’ve probably met her too, right? After saying just a few words, she hangs up. She’s busy taking care of the child every day and hasn’t shown up at the office for a long time.
Respondent: Why are you looking for her?
Respondent: As long as we don’t receive complaints, it’s fine, but when the police come, it’s a bit...
Respondent: Besides, she’s not the type to slack off while working:
